story.lore.l19.title: Mei's Route Correction
story.lore.l19.body:
The new gate stands on the east wall, but the stairs reach it from the west. Draw the path people can walk, not the direction the wall faces.

The ledge under the second rail sounds hollow. Put the lamp before the turn, not at the gate itself. If someone can already see the gate, they have passed the bad step.

No running in a line. Let the slower person lead until the landing, then make room.

To whoever copies this: keep the untidy arrow. It goes around a place your ruler will make look straight.
story.lore.l20.title: Handover Form, Unused
story.lore.l20.body:
A handover is complete only when the incoming workers have read the limits, tested the shutdown, and stated which duties they can accept.

Fields: name; duty; interval; relief contact; refusal and withdrawal procedure; date of next review.

The outgoing worker does not become the relief contact by default.

If no person can take the whole assignment, divide the assignment. If it cannot be divided safely, redesign it before asking again.

The paper has not yellowed evenly. Its outer edges were exposed for years; the center was protected beneath the renewal stack.
story.lore.l21.title: First Week: Open Water
story.lore.l21.body:
The intake is open for two morning intervals. The apprentice will check the governor between them. Nobody should wait beside the binding for a response; the old warden is released.

The lower wheel turned yesterday. Its keeper sent a sack of flour, and a note asking whether the winter interval would be longer. We have not promised that yet.

Lan has written a list of other people who can learn the readings. There are only two names. He left room for more.

A new bell thread hangs beside the old one. Neither has been painted gold.
story.lore.l22.title: First Week: The Smaller Gate
story.lore.l22.body:
The mountain intake is sealed and drained. No one is to reopen it to improve the sanctuary's readings.

The western terrace channel passed its first inspection. The two households are staying with neighbours until the new hearths are set. Their furniture is dry; the old walls will be dismantled after the weather clears.

There is no spiritual mist over the practice yard this morning. Training starts at the usual hour.

Lan has taken the ceremonial gate plate down. In its place is a smaller sign: Tools may be borrowed. Return them clean.
story.lore.l22.inspect: Read First Week: The Smaller Gate
story.lore.l23.title: First Week: Shared Reading
story.lore.l23.body:
The first shared reading differed by half a mark. The mountain copy and the mill copy were both kept. After checking the lower step, the readers found silt beneath the float.

The schedule has been amended. Nobody lost their place for bringing a disagreeing number.

One household has withdrawn from night duty for the planting month. The relief worker signed beside the change. The river did not need a prisoner to keep flowing.

The apprentice will join the next inspection as a worker, not as the only person whose absence stops the world.
story.lore.l24.title: The New Apprentice Column
story.lore.l24.body:
A supply porter has asked whether there is room to learn here.

The practice sword is still the plain one. The apprentice who carried it last has sharpened it and shortened the binding so smaller hands can hold it without slipping.

In the new register, the lesson begins with a route inspection. The cultivation columns come later. Beside the place for a master's seal, someone has added a place for the student's questions.

Lan left the fee column blank. He has written GUTTERS in the margin, then crossed it out and written ONLY IF THEY NEED CLEARING.
